newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia sees security, economic benefit of ASEAN.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia sees security, economic benefit of ASEAN.

text.p: Cambodia's newly appointed First Prime Minister Ung Huot said on Friday he was hopeful Cambodia would become a member of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) before the end of the year.

Cambodia was due to become a full ASEAN member in late July, but the grouping postponed Cambodia's membership indefinitely in response to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's overthrow of his former co-premier, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, on July 6.

Ung Huot, who is also foreign minister, told a seminar on ASEAN that he was hopeful Cambodia would be admitted to the group soon, and he looked forward to both the security and economic benefits of membership.
"I am happy and hopeful to say that before the end of this year, Cambodia will be part of the ASEAN family," Ung Huot told the seminar.
Ung Huot said Cambodia had in the past had disputes with its neighbours, and he was hopeful that membership of ASEAN would prevent the occurrence of such problems in future.
"I do believe that involvement with ASEAN has caused countries with long standing hostilities to put aside their mistrust and dispel their misunderstandings," he said.

"Even if joining the group provides us with not a single dollar of revenue from trade or a single additional piece of foreign investment, this reason alone would make the cost of membership worth it a hundred times over," he said.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Burma, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Ung Huot was upbeat about Cambodia's economic prospects as a member of the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) in spite of the damage to investor confidence caused by the recent fighting and coup.

"Despite the recent event, our welcoming stance towards business and our inclusion in AFTA makes us set to take off into newly industrialised status at a speed perhaps even faster than the record setting rates already achieved by other ASEAN nations," he said.

"We believe that now that the economies of other ASEAN nations are progressively moving towards more highly skilled and capital intensive modes of production, Cambodia can provide a stable and hospitable venue for light industry that is no longer as cost effective in other countries of the region," he said.
ASEAN diplomats have said Cambodia could be admitted to the grouping at a group summit meeting in December.
